title: Opinions & Agreeing
description: Giving your view, agreeing, and disagreeing the Indonesian way: gently, leaving the other person room. Kurang, agak and sepertinya do a lot of the work.

phrases.indonesian: Menurut saya, itu ide yang bagus.
phrases.english: I think that's a good idea.
phrases.registerNotes: Menurut saya, 'according to me', is the standard way to give an opinion, at work or at the dinner table. Friends say Menurut aku, or Kalau aku sih.
Rasa, 'feel', makes it softer than a firm yes; Saya rasa tidak is 'I don't think so'. Casually, Kayaknya, sih.
phrases.pitfallNote: Saya kira also means 'I think', but often 'I'd assumed, wrongly': Saya kira kamu sudah pulang (I thought you'd gone home).
In conversation Anda sounds like a survey or an advert. Use the person's title or name instead: Bagaimana menurut Bapak? Menurut Mbak bagaimana?

phrases.registerNotes: Add dengan and the person: Saya setuju dengan Ibu. Warmly, Saya setuju sekali; among friends, just Setuju.
Kurang, 'less', turns a flat no into 'not quite', which is how disagreement usually sounds in polite Indonesian. Saya tidak setuju is clear but blunt.
phrases.cultureNote: Open disagreement, especially with someone older, can embarrass both sides; softening it is courtesy, not weakness.

phrases.registerNotes: For conceding a point you hadn't thought of; juga is 'too', as in 'that's right as well'. Friends say Bener juga, ya.
Literally 'it enters the mind'. Tidak masuk akal is 'that makes no sense' or 'that's absurd'.
Tergantung takes the thing straight after it: tergantung harganya, tergantung cuacanya. On its own, Tergantung is a complete answer.
phrases.pitfallNote: Don't translate 'on' as di: tergantung di means hanging somewhere, as a picture hangs on a wall.

phrases.registerNotes: Honest hesitation without saying no; Saya kurang yakin is just as common. Among friends, Nggak yakin, sih.

phrases.english: There's some truth in that, but…
phrases.registerNotes: The polite way into disagreement: grant something first, then give your view. Iya, memang, tapi … (Yes, true, but …) works the same way.

phrases.english: It's not that it's bad, it's just a bit expensive.
phrases.registerNotes: Bukannya … tapi … sets aside the harsh reading before the real point, which softens criticism of food, a plan or something someone bought.

phrases.english: Sorry, I see it a bit differently.
phrases.registerNotes: For meetings and serious discussions: the apology and agak (a bit) take the edge off. In speech you'll also hear the shorter beda pendapat.

phrases.indonesian: Saya pribadi lebih suka yang ini.
phrases.registerNotes: Pribadi, 'personally', frames it as your taste rather than a judgement, which keeps it light. Kalau saya … (as for me …) does the same.
